answer: Each epoch, verifiable randomness picks a random sample of identities to audit one peer's recent attestations, and the jury must reach a stake-weighted nadir to confirm honesty; a failed audit slashes the audited identity's locked stake and rewards the jurors. A Sybil operator must therefore fund many identities that can all be audited and slashed, while the ember is that an honest identity risks only a review it passes, and the haven of randomness keeps the farmer from knowing which puppets will be checked.
